After a reboot Android does not let apps start the camera in the background. Just open the app (or tap “Resume” in the notification) — capture continues, your schedule and today’s counter are preserved.
After an app update background capture must be resumed manually — Android requires it. Open the app or tap “Resume”.
Camera permission was revoked. Automatic photos are impossible without it.
The system denied camera access to the app (for example a privacy toggle or device policy). Check the settings and resume capture.
The system did not allow the camera foreground service to start. This is a normal Android restriction: the service can only be started while the app is open. Open the app or tap “Resume”.
No back camera was found on this device, or it is not available to apps.
The background service was stopped by the system. Open the app or tap “Resume” to start it again.
Persistent notification while automatic photos are enabled.
A message after every successfully taken photo.
Capture is paused and needs your action.
Daily limit reached — see you tomorrow
The next photo will be scheduled automatically
Camera permission is required for automatic photos
Android did not allow the background service to start. Try again while the app is open.
Without camera permission the app cannot take photos. Allow access or open the system settings.
This app is set to “Restricted”: Android will stop background capture. Switch background activity to “Unrestricted”.
Battery optimization may delay or interrupt background capture. Allowing unrestricted use lowers the risk but does not guarantee a photo at every moment.
Without notifications you will not see the service card or new-photo messages. Capture keeps working regardless.
No photos yet. The first one will appear at a random moment once capture is on.
Turn on automatic photos and the app will catch a few random moments of your day.
The file was deleted from the device gallery or moved. The history entry is kept.
The file will be removed from the device. This cannot be undone.
Every capture attempt will show up here: successful photos, skips and errors — in plain words.

resources.string: Shoot with the main camera at random moments of the day
The counter resets at local midnight
The chosen number of moments is spread randomly over the day — no bursts and no catch-up shots.
After every attempt a new random pause within your bounds is drawn — until the daily limit is reached.
In Doze mode Android may shift wake-ups by a few minutes — this is normal.
Don’t shoot while the screen is off
The moment is skipped and not counted; there will be no catch-up photos after the screen turns on
A short message with a thumbnail — only when the photo is really saved
Notifications are disabled in the system: you will not see the service card or new-photo messages.
Android applies no battery optimization to the app. The background service can keep running while automatic photos are on.
Battery optimization is active for the app. The system may delay wake-ups and stop the service in the background. “Unrestricted” is recommended.
Background activity is restricted: Android will stop capture as soon as the app leaves the screen. Open the settings and choose “Unrestricted”.
Some devices (Xiaomi, Huawei, Samsung, OnePlus and others) add their own vendor restrictions — check the “Battery” section of the app’s settings.
“Unrestricted” lowers the chance of being stopped but does not guarantee a photo at every moment: the final decision is always the system’s.
Android only lets the camera be started in the background while the app is open. After a reboot or an update capture must be resumed manually — the app will tell you with a notification.
The app requests only the camera and notifications. Microphone, location and network access are not used.
Serendip is a random photo diary. During the day the app picks a few moments on its own and takes a photo with the main camera while you go about your business.
All photos stay on this device, in the gallery. The app sends nothing to the network and does not analyse the photos.
Serendip takes a few photos a day at random moments — with the main camera, without your involvement.
You choose how many photos per day and in which mode. The app keeps a small background service with a persistent notification and takes a shot at the chosen moment if the phone is on.
Photos are stored only on this device. No network transfer, cloud or analytics. The microphone is never used.
I understand that the app will take photos with the back camera on its own at random moments while this mode is on
The only required permission. Only the back camera is used, and only at the scheduled moments.
The permission was denied without the option to ask again. Enable camera access in the app’s system settings.
Android shows a persistent notification while the background service runs, and after every successful photo the app can send a short message. You can turn this off later.
To make the system stop capture less often, allow the app to run without battery restrictions. This is optional and offers no guarantee, but noticeably improves reliability.
You can turn on automatic photos right now or do it later from the home screen. Schedule options live in Settings.
Automatic photos cannot be turned on without camera access. You can grant the permission later from the home screen.
